sentences.en: I'm Jenna Fisher.
And I'm Angela Kinsey.
We were on The Office together.
sentences.zh: 我们曾一起出演《办公室》。

sentences.en: And we're best friends.
And now we're doing the Ultimate Office rewatch podcast just for you.
sentences.zh: 现在我们正为你们制作终极《办公室》重温播客。

sentences.en: Each week, we will break down an episode of The Office and give exclusive behind-the-scenes stories that only two people who were there can tell you.
sentences.zh: 每周，我们都会解析一集《办公室》，并分享只有身临其境的两人才能告诉你的独家幕后故事。

sentences.en: We're The Office Ladies.
I hope you're in a festive mood today because we're talking about Moroccan Christmas.
sentences.zh: 希望你今天心情不错，因为我们要聊的是“摩洛哥圣诞节”。

sentences.en: So get out your Christmas plaid, but put away that nativity scene because Phyllis is going to throw you the party of a lifetime.
sentences.zh: 所以拿出你的圣诞格子衫，但把那个耶稣诞生场景收起来，因为菲利斯要为你举办一场终生难忘的派对。

sentences.en: She sure is.
It's Season 5, Episode 11, written by Justin Spitzer and directed by Paul Feig.
sentences.zh: 这是第五季第11集，由贾斯汀·斯皮策编剧，保罗·费格执导。

sentences.en: Here is your summary.
As you said, Phyllis throws a Moroccan-themed Christmas party, which receives compliments from the majority of the group, but some serious contempt from Angela.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，菲利斯举办了一场摩洛哥主题的圣诞派对，大多数人都称赞有加，但安吉拉却表现出极大的蔑视。

sentences.en: Oh, she is not happy.
Dwight runs a black market doll trade out of The Office.
sentences.zh: 德怀特在办公室里经营着黑市玩偶交易。

sentences.en: And Meredith gets wasted and sets herself on fire.
sentences.zh: 梅雷迪思喝得烂醉，还把自己点着了。

sentences.en: That's a doozy of a sentence.
It's quite a work party.
sentences.zh: 这真是一场特别的职场派对。

sentences.en: Michael decides to hold an intervention demanding Meredith get help for her alcoholism.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔决定举行一次干预行动，要求梅雷迪思为她的酗酒问题寻求帮助。

sentences.en: And then, talk about a doozy of a work party.
sentences.zh: 说到信息量大的职场派对，这绝对算一个。

sentences.en: Ugh.
Phyllis spills the beans about Angela and Dwight in front of everyone.
sentences.zh: 菲利斯在所有人面前泄露了安吉拉和德怀特的事。

sentences.en: Everyone!
She announces it to the whole bullpen!
sentences.zh: 她向整个办公区宣布了这件事！

sentences.en: Except Andy.
Oh, Andy.
Yeah.
Andy in a sitar.
His goodbye as he's leaving broke my heart.
sentences.zh: 他离开时的告别让我心碎。

sentences.en: We're getting ahead.
We're getting ahead.
We're getting ahead.

Fast fact number one.
This was the third Christmas-themed episode of The Office.
sentences.zh: 这是《办公室》的第三集圣诞主题剧集。

sentences.en: Yes, it was.
Season five, but only three Christmas episodes.
sentences.zh: 虽然是第五季，但只有三集圣诞特辑。

sentences.en: Why?
Well, the first season, we didn't have one.
sentences.zh: 嗯，第一季的时候我们没有拍。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
And then, in season four, it was the writer's strike.
sentences.zh: 然后，第四季的时候碰上了编剧罢工。

sentences.en: I know.
We missed a Christmas party.
sentences.zh: 我们错过了一场圣诞派对。

sentences.en: It has been two years since we had a Christmas party on The Office.
sentences.zh: 距离我们在《办公室》里举办圣诞派对已经过去两年了。

sentences.en: They were always some of my favorite episodes, so I was excited.
sentences.zh: 它们一直是我最喜欢的剧集之一，所以我很兴奋。

sentences.en: Me too.
I liked them because they were majority group scenes.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢它们是因为它们大部分都是集体戏。

sentences.en: Yes.
We were all together all the time.
It was like a whole episode of Conference Room.
sentences.zh: 就像整集都在会议室里一样。

sentences.en: So, lots of bits.
Lots of bits.
Lots of laughing.
We would just have the best time.
sentences.zh: 我们当时真的玩得特别开心。

sentences.en: We would get loopy.
sentences.zh: 我们当时都疯疯癫癫的。

sentences.en: We would.
But in the best way.
Fast fact number two.
The inspiration for this episode, I was able to get in touch with writer Justin Spitzer.
sentences.zh: 关于这一集的灵感来源，我联系上了编剧贾斯汀·斯皮策。

sentences.en: What'd Justin have to say?
He told me that they had had these two ideas rolling around for a really long time.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我，他们脑子里一直酝酿着两个点子，已经很久了。

sentences.en: The first one was the idea of a Moroccan Christmas.
sentences.zh: 第一个点子是关于摩洛哥圣诞节。

sentences.en: They just loved the idea that Phyllis had thrown that amazing goodbye party for Toby.
sentences.zh: 他们特别喜欢菲利斯为托比举办的那场精彩告别派对的构思。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
And that maybe the success had gone to her head a little bit.
sentences.zh: 而且觉得那次成功可能让她有点飘了。

sentences.en: And she's going to go big.
Big theme.
Yes.
They loved that this would piss Angela off.
sentences.zh: 他们很喜欢这个点子，因为这会让安吉拉气炸。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
So, this was like one card.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就像是一张卡片上的内容。

sentences.en: Right.
You know what the card probably said?
sentences.zh: 你知道那张卡片上可能写了什么吗？

sentences.en: What?
Phyllis happy Angela pissed.
sentences.zh: 菲利斯开心，安吉拉气炸。

sentences.en: Christmas.
Question mark.
Why is your character always so angry on Christmas?
sentences.zh: 为什么你的角色在圣诞节总是那么生气？

sentences.en: She's angry all the time.
But it really comes out at the holidays.
sentences.zh: 但在节日期间表现得尤为明显。

sentences.en: She has levels of anger.
Sometimes she's like suspicious bitch.
sentences.zh: 有时她是那种多疑的贱人。

sentences.en: Sometimes she's happy bitch.
sentences.zh: 有时她是那种开心的贱人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
Sometimes she's sad bitch.
sentences.zh: 有时她是那种悲伤的贱人。

sentences.en: Hmm.
And then Christmas bitch is a whole different bitch.
sentences.zh: 而圣诞节的贱人则是完全不同的一种贱人。

sentences.en: Oh, boy.
Buckle in for Christmas bitch.
sentences.zh: 做好准备迎接圣诞节贱人吧。

sentences.en: Okay.
So, the other card that they had on the wall for a really long time said Meredith Intervention.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们墙上挂了很久的另一张卡片写的是：梅雷迪思干预行动。

sentences.en: Oh, okay.
So, they decided to marry these two ideas.
sentences.zh: 于是，他们决定把这两个点子结合起来。

sentences.en: Remember when they did like Michael has to fire someone on Halloween while we're all dressed up?
sentences.zh: 还记得他们拍过迈克尔必须在万圣节解雇某人，而我们都穿着戏服的那一集吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
It's the same thing.
Yes.
Exactly.
Justin said that a holiday party also seemed like a really good place for Meredith to drink too much and set her hair on fire.
sentences.zh: 贾斯汀说，节日派对似乎也是梅雷迪思喝多并烧着头发的好时机。

sentences.en: Like, there could be this sort of rock-bottomy moment.
sentences.zh: 就像是，可以出现那种跌入谷底的时刻。

sentences.en: Right.
And it's an event.
It's like a big event and everyone's there to witness it.
sentences.zh: 就像一场大型活动，每个人都在现场见证。

sentences.en: Yes.
Fast fact number three, I have a talking head observation for this episode.
sentences.zh: 第三个冷知识，关于这一集，我有一个关于“访谈”镜头的发现。

sentences.en: Oh, I'm so curious.
So, as you re-watch this episode, take a note of the talking heads.
sentences.zh: 所以，当你重温这一集时，留意一下那些访谈镜头。

sentences.en: Almost all of them are filmed from different angles than we normally would.
sentences.zh: 几乎所有的镜头拍摄角度都和我们平时拍的不一样。

sentences.en: I believe there's only one where someone's seated in the traditional chair with the kind of party through the blind.
sentences.zh: 我记得只有一个镜头是有人坐在传统的椅子上，背景是那种百叶窗。

sentences.en: Right.
Right.
We're all over the office.
sentences.zh: 我们当时在办公室各处拍摄。

sentences.en: All over the office.
So, this was not just because there was a party happening behind us.
sentences.zh: 所以，这不仅仅是因为我们身后正在举办派对。

sentences.en: Justin said this was because they wanted to wait until they were in the editing room to place the talking heads throughout the episode.
sentences.zh: 贾斯汀说这是因为他们想等到剪辑室里，再决定把这些访谈镜头安插在这一集的什么位置。

sentences.en: And they didn't want anything in the background to, like, in some way, mess up their ability to move these talking heads around.
sentences.zh: 他们不想让背景里的任何东西，以某种方式影响他们随意移动这些访谈镜头。

sentences.en: Well, they had probably learned their lesson from that episode, Weight Loss.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们大概是从“减肥”那一集吸取了教训。

sentences.en: Yeah.
Where they had to digitally, it's a hard word to say, they had to digitally change Ed's tie and shirt.
sentences.zh: 在那一集里，他们不得不——这个词很难念——他们不得不通过数字技术修改了艾德的领带和衬衫。

sentences.en: Yeah.
So, they kept moving the talking heads and what was happening behind them didn't match.
sentences.zh: 因为他们一直在移动访谈镜头，导致背景里发生的事情对不上。

sentences.en: Yeah.
So, you'll notice even Michael's talking heads, he is not seated at his desk.
sentences.zh: 所以你会注意到，连迈克尔的访谈镜头里，他都没有坐在办公桌前。

sentences.en: He's standing in front of his desk and they purposely framed out the window behind him because timing-wise, they didn't know if it would be, like,
sentences.zh: 他是站在办公桌前的，而且他们特意避开了他身后的窗户，因为从时间安排上来说，他们不知道到时候会是，比如，

sentences.en: still daytime or if it would be evening.
So, they really tried to make all the talking heads as totally neutral as possible.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们真的尽量让所有的访谈镜头都保持绝对的中性。

sentences.en: Smart.
Yeah.
And it was kind of fun.
After Justin told me that, I went back and re-watched the episode and it was totally true.
sentences.zh: 贾斯汀告诉我之后，我回去重看了这一集，发现确实如此。

sentences.en: Yeah.
I read the shooting draft and definitely things are moved all around.
sentences.zh: 我读了拍摄剧本，确实有很多地方被挪动了。

sentences.en: So, it's good they did it.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们这么做是对的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
That's all I got.
sentences.zh: 这就是我所有的发现了。

sentences.en: Well, before we get into this episode, I went digging in my digital clutter.
sentences.zh: 好吧，在进入这一集之前，我翻了翻我的电子文档。

sentences.en: Okay.
And I found an email from Paul Feig that on December 11th, 2008, he emailed the group, Jenna,
sentences.zh: 我找到了一封保罗·费格在2008年12月11日发给我们的邮件，珍娜，

sentences.en: and invited us all to a Christmas taco party to watch the Moroccan Christmas episode at his house.
sentences.zh: 他邀请我们所有人去他家参加圣诞塔可派对，一起看“摩洛哥圣诞”那一集。

sentences.en: Oh.
And he said, I know, I know, Morocco and tacos make no sense, except they do kind of rhyme and we have a really great taco cart that we want to use.
sentences.zh: 他说，我知道，我知道，摩洛哥和塔可（墨西哥夹饼）完全不搭，但它们听起来有点押韵，而且我们有一个很棒的塔可餐车想用一下。

sentences.en: And we all went over to his house December 11th, 2008, and watched Moroccan Christmas together.
sentences.zh: 于是我们都在2008年12月11日去了他家，一起看了“摩洛哥圣诞”。

sentences.en: Aw, I love that you brought that up because Paul and Lori Feig used to host so many viewing parties at their house and they were just the most wonderful hosts.
sentences.zh: 噢，我很高兴你提到了这个，因为保罗和洛里·费格过去常在他们家举办观影派对，他们真是最棒的主人。

sentences.en: And I'll never forget, he had that screen that would come down from the ceiling.
sentences.zh: 我永远不会忘记，他有一个会从天花板降下来的屏幕。

sentences.en: So, he had like a very normal looking living room.
sentences.zh: 所以，他的客厅看起来非常普通。

sentences.en: Yeah.
Cozy, like a place you'd read books.
sentences.zh: 很温馨，就像那种你会读书的地方。

sentences.en: I believe there was like a green leather chair.
sentences.zh: 我记得好像有一把绿色皮椅子。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
There was like cozy chairs with like a blanket draped over it.
sentences.zh: 还有那种舒适的椅子，上面还搭着毯子。

sentences.en: So cozy, and then all of a sudden when it was time to watch the show, the screen would come down out of the ceiling and it would turn into this amazing viewing experience.
sentences.zh: 非常舒适，然后突然间，当到了看节目的时候，屏幕就会从天花板上降下来，变成一种令人惊叹的观影体验。

sentences.en: I thought, these guys are doing it right.
sentences.zh: 我想，这些人真是做对了。

sentences.en: They know what they're doing.
Yeah.
And they have a great taco cart.
sentences.zh: 而且他们还有很棒的塔可餐车。

sentences.en: Aw, that's so cool.
Well, there you go.
Just a little something from my digital clutter.
sentences.zh: 只是我数字杂物里的一点小东西。

sentences.en: And now, we should break down this episode.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们该剖析这一集了。

sentences.en: Well, I think we should take a break firSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我觉得我们应该先休息一下。

sentences.en: And now, we should take a break.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们该休息一下了。

sentences.en: Let's do it, and we'll be back to talk all things Moroccan Christmas.
sentences.zh: 就这样吧，回来后我们要聊聊关于“摩洛哥圣诞节”的一切。

sentences.en: Well, we are back.
And wow, is Dwight's desk festive or what?
sentences.zh: 哇，德怀特的办公桌是不是很有节日气氛？

sentences.en: Oh, my.
This is an epic prank by Jim.
sentences.zh: 这是吉姆的一个史诗级恶作剧。

sentences.en: Every single thing on Dwight's desk is wrapped in Christmas wrapping paper.
sentences.zh: 德怀特桌上的每一件东西都用圣诞包装纸包起来了。

sentences.en: Including his chair.
Yeah.
When did Jim do this?
How long did it take?
What the heck?
I have so much to share about this.
sentences.zh: 关于这个我有很多想分享的。

sentences.en: Oh, go.
All right.
First of all, Justin Spitzer told me this was his idea.
sentences.zh: 首先，贾斯汀·斯皮策告诉我这是他的主意。

sentences.en: This was his pitch.
He said that he was always talking to his friends who worked in the corporate world.
sentences.zh: 他说他总是和在企业界工作的朋友聊天。

sentences.en: And he would ask them, what sort of pranks go on in your office?
sentences.zh: 他会问他们，你们办公室里有什么样的恶作剧？

sentences.en: Because I think at a certain point, it started to stress out the writers that they had to come up with these Jim Dwight pranks.
sentences.zh: 因为我觉得在某个阶段，编剧们必须想出这些吉姆整蛊德怀特的恶作剧，这让他们感到压力很大。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
So they were always fishing.
sentences.zh: 所以他们总是在搜罗素材。

sentences.en: Tell me a prank.
I need an office prank.
sentences.zh: 我需要一个办公室恶作剧。

sentences.en: He said that the single most mentioned prank was this idea of wrapping someone's desk in paper or aluminum foil.
sentences.zh: 他说被提到次数最多的恶作剧就是把某人的办公桌用纸或铝箔纸包起来。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
So Justin pitched this idea.
sentences.zh: 所以贾斯汀提出了这个想法。

sentences.en: We got so much mail from people asking, how did we pull this off?
sentences.zh: 我们收到了很多观众来信，问我们是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: I reached out to Randy Cordray.
Oh, Randy.
He shared all the details.
Of course he did.
And then he probably did a deep dive for you on something random.
sentences.zh: 然后他可能还为你深入挖掘了一些随机的事情。

sentences.en: He did.
All those things.
So, first of all, he said there was a note in the script that did not make it into the episode, and it was a Jim talking head, and here's how it went.
sentences.zh: 所以，首先，他说剧本里有一段没能出现在正片里的备注，那是吉姆的采访片段，内容是这样的。

sentences.en: Jim says,
Actually, it took me about a week to recreate the desk and chair in chicken wire.
sentences.zh: 其实，我花了一周时间用铁丝网重现了桌子和椅子。

sentences.en: I had to come in about four hours early and set it all up, and I think I pulled something in my back, dragging Dwight's real desk all the way up to the roof.
sentences.zh: 我不得不提前四个小时来布置这一切，我想我在把德怀特真正的办公桌拖到屋顶时，拉伤了背部。

sentences.en: All for a three-second payoff.
sentences.zh: 这一切只为了三秒钟的笑点。

sentences.en: Totally worth it.
I read that, too, and I was like, why do you have to take the desk up to the roof?
sentences.zh: 我也读过那段，当时我就想，为什么非要把桌子搬到屋顶上去？

sentences.en: Why couldn't you just stash it in the warehouse?
sentences.zh: 为什么不能直接把它藏在仓库里？

sentences.en: I swear I remember us filming a tag of Dwight working up on the roof.
sentences.zh: 我发誓我记得我们拍过一个德怀特在屋顶上干活的片尾彩蛋。

sentences.en: Oh, my gosh.
I swear we did.
I can't confirm it, but I feel like I remember what, you know, you're walking from your trailer to hair and makeup, and you're like, why are they putting a desk on the roof?
sentences.zh: 我没法证实，但我感觉我记得那种场景，你知道的，你从拖车走到化妆间，然后你会想，他们为什么要把桌子放在屋顶上？

sentences.en: I have a hazy memory of this.
sentences.zh: 我对这件事有点模糊的记忆。

sentences.en: What else did Randy say?
All right, so Randy also said that Greg Daniels was pretty insistent that the gag desk be made out of chicken wire because that's what it said in the script.
sentences.zh: 好吧，兰迪还说格雷格·丹尼尔斯非常坚持要用铁丝网做那个恶作剧桌子，因为剧本里就是这么写的。

sentences.en: Oh, and he wanted it exactly like that.
sentences.zh: 噢，他想要完全符合剧本的那种。

sentences.en: Yeah, because we'd sort of, Jim has this whole speech.
sentences.zh: 是啊，因为我们当时，吉姆有一大段演讲。

sentences.en: He's like, it needs to reflect what Jim said.
sentences.zh: 他说，这必须反映出吉姆所说的话。

sentences.en: But chicken wire is stronger than you think.
sentences.zh: 但铁丝网比你想象的要结实。

sentences.en: Oh, yes, it is.
Right?
It wouldn't have collapsed.
Nope.
It wouldn't have, Ange.
Did they make one with chicken wire and it didn't work?
sentences.zh: 他们是不是用铁丝网做了一个，结果没成功？

sentences.en: So Randy said that he and Paul Feig and our set designer, Michael Gallenberg, and our first AD, Kelly Cantley, all tried to talk Greg out of this.
sentences.zh: 兰迪说他和保罗·费格、我们的布景设计师迈克尔·加伦伯格，还有我们的第一副导演凯莉·坎特利，都试图劝格雷格放弃这个想法。

sentences.en: They were very skeptical it would work, but Greg really needed to see it for himself.
sentences.zh: 他们对这是否可行非常怀疑，但格雷格真的需要亲眼看看才行。

sentences.en: Okay.
So here's what they did.
They built four different desks out of four different materials.
sentences.zh: 他们用四种不同的材料做了四张不同的桌子。

sentences.en: Oh, my gosh.
What were the materials?
One of them was chicken wire.
Okay.
One was styrofoam.
Ew.
One was balsa wood.
What?
And one was corrugated cardboard.
And then they meticulously gift-wrapped all of them.
sentences.zh: 然后他们一丝不苟地把它们全都包装成了礼物。

sentences.en: Ooh, ooh.
Can I guess?
Can I guess which one worked the best?
sentences.zh: 我能猜猜哪个效果最好吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
What do you guys think?
